title: Decompose continuous runloop into explicit stages and add KV lease facade
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: The continuous batching runloop and KV cache lifecycle are currently implemented as a single monolithic event loop. This has made targeted optimizations (e.g. lightweight windowing vs commit-critical paths) difficult and introduces inadvertent contention between admission, prefetch, and eviction logic. We've observed tail-latency spikes during mixed workloads and have multiple heatmaps indicating cross-path mutex contention in the runloop thread.

Problem: Ongoing performance work is hampered by the coupling between: 1) admission/token-windowing, 2) batch assembly and prefetch triggers, and 3) commit/lease renewal + KV eviction. Hotfixes only address symptoms. We need a refactor that separates concerns, reduces lock granularity, and provides a stable abstraction for KV leases so other teams can safely build on top of the cache without reintroducing contention.
proposal: 1) Decompose the continuous runloop into three explicit stages with clear contracts: ingress (request aggregation/admission), windowing/assembly (batch formation, prefetch kickoffs), and commit/lease (final commit, KV lease renewals, eviction signals). 2) Introduce a KV lease facade (kv-lease-facade) that standardizes lease acquisition, heartbeating, and safe renew/failover semantics across shards. The facade will expose a non-blocking API for fast-path reads and a lease-management API for commit paths. 3) Migrate the compact KV index to use a small sharded epoch map per shard to reduce global metadata contention. 4) Add lightweight stage-level metrics and SLO guards so we can circuit-break the commit stage if latency or error budget is violated. 5) Implement the changes behind a runtime feature flag with a canary rollout to a single tenant pool and synthetic load tests prior to broader rollout.
alternatives_considered: Do nothing and continue targeted hotfixes (rejected - high tech debt and recurrent regressions)
Full rewrite of the batcher in coroutine runtime (rejected - risky and high effort for short-term wins)
Introduce per-request worker threads to isolate commit (rejected - increases memory footprint and scheduling overhead)
acceptance_criteria: Runloop is split and each stage has clear, documented contracts in code and Confluence
KV lease facade implemented and used by commit path; facade tests cover expire/steal/renew scenarios
Unit and integration tests validating semantics for prefetch vs commit race conditions
Canary tenant shows no >2% increase in p99 tail latency and at least 10% reduction in lock contention metrics
Migration of compact KV index to sharded epoch map reduces global mutex hold time in flamegraphs by >=30%
Feature flag supports on/off switching without requiring node restart and no client-visible errors when toggled
tasks: Spec: write runloop stage contracts and diagrams (Confluence)
Implement ingress stage: extract admission/token-windowing logic into StageIngress module
Implement windowing stage: batch assembly + prefetch triggers in StageWindowing
Implement commit stage: lease interactions and eviction signals in StageCommit
Implement kv-lease-facade with non-blocking read path and lease manager subcomponent
Migrate compact KV index to sharded epoch map and add background compaction task
Add stage-level metrics (latency, queue depth, error rate) and SLO guards
Write unit + integration tests for stage boundaries and kv-lease-facade
Create canary job and synthetic bench harness reproducing mixed-seq-length workload
Roll out behind feature flag to canary pool, monitor, iterate, then widen rollout
test_plan: Unit tests for each stage module covering happy/edge/failure paths
Integration test simulating prefetch vs commit race with injected delays
Load bench: 1000 concurrent streams with token distribution matching production p50/p95
Chaos test: kill lease manager and verify safe failover and no batch duplication
A/B canary: compare p50/p95/p99 token latency and lock contention traces between old and new codepaths
monitoring_runbook: If canary p99 increases >2% or KV lease error rate >0.5% for 5m: flip feature flag off for that pool, collect CPU flamegraphs and lock contention profiles, capture recent commits and prefetch traces, and page oncall (runtime-sre). If eviction storms occur, disable automatic eviction and revert to previous compaction configuration.
rollout_plan: Deploy as opt-in feature flag in staging and run bench for 24h
Canary: enable for single low-traffic tenant pool for 72h with synthetic load
Monitor metrics and perform flamegraph comparison; require sign-off from runtime, SRE, and product
Widen to 10% of serving capacity for 48h, then to 50% for 24h, then global if healthy
Provide immediate rollback path via feature flag and deployment automation
comments: 2026-03-01 - Jonah Martinez: Spiked a decomposition locally. Ingress/windowing split looks feasible; commit stage still has a handful of cross-shard touches to eliminate.

2026-03-08 - Priya Singh (Runtime): Reviewed facade proposal. Suggested making heartbeating pluggable for dedicated deployments that prefer external KMS locks.
2026-03-12 - Jonah Martinez: Initial implementation of StageIngress landed in draft PR. Running unit tests and profiling in staging cluster.
2026-03-14 - SRE Review: Observability hooks added. Can we add a histogram for lease acquisition latency? Filing follow-up task if needed.
